definition: Symbiosis means a close, ongoing relationship in which each side depends on the other and both benefit.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word symbiosis. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know symbiosis should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The lichen crusting the boulder is a symbiosis you can hold: a fungus that shelters an alga, and an alga that feeds the fungus.
Cooperation is weaker than symbiosis: cooperating parties work together while staying fully separate, but symbiosis means the two lives have grown intertwined, each depending on the other.
Fusion goes further than symbiosis — in symbiosis the two partners stay distinct while depending on each other; in a fusion the boundary dissolves and only one merged thing remains.

Mutualism is biology's narrow term for a two-species relationship in which both organisms gain. Symbiosis is the broader, more common word, and it travels outside the lab — businesses, neighborhoods, and art forms can live in symbiosis too.
A partnership is a deliberate arrangement to work together, and either partner can walk away from it whole. Symbiosis adds real dependence: pull the two apart and each one is worse off.

Every March, beekeeper Rosa Delgado trucks two hundred hives into the almond orchards outside Chico, and the growers open their gates before dawn.
The arrangement looks like a simple rental, but the growers describe it as symbiosis, and the account books bear them out.
Without the bees, the orchards set almost no fruit; the harvest that pays the growers' loans depends on three weeks of pollination.
Without the almond bloom, Rosa's colonies would starve through early spring, when nothing else within range flowers.
Her strongest hives are built on almond nectar.
Neither side chose to need the other, and neither can leave whole.
When a late frost thinned the bloom two years ago, growers and beekeepers lost the season together.
